docs.title: AI SDLC Loop
docs.text:
Ship a bounded change through Specify → Implement → Verify with explicit approval before code mutation and commit.

AI SDLC Loop is the focused delivery member of the AI SDLC product family. It installs 18 working ai-sdlc-loop-{slug} skills and one shared runtime while keeping decisions and evidence in deterministic local TOON artifacts.

Start with a project-scoped install Read the workflow model

docs.title: Why use it?
docs.text:
• Keep implementation and commit authority behind separate explicit approvals.
  • Bound source changes to declared repository paths.
  • Run verification through explicit argv-safe commands.
  • Preserve redacted, deterministic evidence without runtime telemetry.
  • Promote supported results into AI SDLC Harness workflows.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Install for a Codex project:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikegorelikoff/ai-sdlc-loop/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- codex-project

Verify in a separate step:

python3 .ai-sdlc-loop/install/install.py verify codex-project

The installer preserves unrelated skills and writes a TOON inventory below .ai-sdlc-loop/install/.

docs.title: AI SDLC product family
docs.text:
Structure delivery. Control context. Measure adoption.

  • AI SDLC Harness structures the broader delivery lifecycle.
  • AI SDLC Loop provides the smaller approval-gated delivery cycle.
  • Context Guard controls avoidable context growth.
  • AI SDLC Metrics measures local adoption evidence.

The products are complementary and independently installed.

docs.title: Authority and evidence
docs.text:
Loop distinguishes evidence from authority. A fingerprint proves that inputs match a previously reviewed value; it is not identity or permission. A TOON approval receipt records a decision but does not bypass repository policy, the execution sandbox, or host confirmation.

Flow may select an owner. Doctor may recommend remediation. Neither may mutate source, install packages, or execute the selected owner action. Implement and Commit enforce their own current receipts. Verification records command results but cannot retroactively authorize a command.

Git remains authoritative for repository state. Loop preserves unrelated tracked, staged, unstaged, and untracked work.

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
After the canonical installation and verification, ask the agent to use ai-sdlc-loop-flow with a bounded outcome, feature slug, and relevant paths. Explore explains the route without writing files. Review the owning skill and planned writes before Apply or any downstream approval.

The first protected source mutation still requires the Implement approval owned by Loop. A later commit requires its own current approval.

Follow Deliver a first change for the full procedure.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Loop separates lifecycle ownership from reusable delivery controls.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. ai-sdlc-loop-flow explores and fingerprints one route; ai-sdlc-loop-orchestrate remains the direct stage router.
  2. ai-sdlc-loop-specify normalizes scope and writes the specification fingerprint.
  3. ai-sdlc-loop-implement checks current approval before source mutation.
  4. ai-sdlc-loop-verify collects command evidence and computes readiness.
  5. ai-sdlc-loop-commit checks a separate current approval before one commit.

docs.title: Delivery controls
docs.text:
Eleven focused skills own approvals, branching, requirements review, test cases, QA, validation, code review, security testing, commit preparation, Conventional Commit validation, and release readiness. They share one standard-library runtime and do not require the full Harness refinement catalog.

ai-sdlc-loop-doctor independently diagnoses the installed inventory and previews non-authorizing upgrade plans. See Flow and Doctor for procedures.

docs.title: Authority model
docs.text:
TOON receipts record explicit decisions against exact fingerprints. They are capability records, not cryptographic identity proofs. A missing, rejected, stale, mismatched, or drifted receipt denies the protected transition.

Git remains authoritative for source state. Loop preserves unrelated tracked, staged, unstaged, and untracked work and refuses changes outside the approved paths.

docs.title: Evidence model
docs.text: Verification executes only declared argv-safe commands without a shell. Evidence includes ordered outcomes, bounded redacted output, hashes, and readiness. Any failed, missing, interrupted, or timed-out required command blocks readiness.

docs.title: Harness compatibility
docs.text: promote validates Loop state and emits ai-sdlc-harness-promotion/v1 TOON. It preserves supported request, path, trace, fingerprint, approval, command, and evidence fields without rewriting Harness state.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
AI SDLC Loop requires Python 3.9 or newer, Git on PATH, and a repository directory where the selected project skill root can be created. The POSIX bootstrap additionally requires curl, tar, and a POSIX shell; native Windows installation uses python install.py.

The installer does not overwrite unmanaged or drifted Loop skills. A custom agent root must be project-relative and cannot overlap .git/ or .ai-sdlc-loop/.

Continue with the canonical Start here path.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: This is the canonical first-run path for AI SDLC Loop.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From the project that should receive the skills, run one command:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikegorelikoff/ai-sdlc-loop/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- codex-project

Then verify separately:

python3 .ai-sdlc-loop/install/install.py verify codex-project

Claude Code projects use claude-code-project. Another compatible agent uses agent-project --skills-root .agent/skills.

docs.title: Run the first loop
docs.text:
Ask the agent to use ai-sdlc-loop-flow for a bounded repository change. Provide the intended outcome and relevant paths. The agent should:

  1. create a deterministic specification and fingerprint;
  2. request approval before implementation;
  3. keep changes inside the approved paths;
  4. run explicit verification commands;
  5. request a separate approval before committing.

docs.title: Expected result
docs.text: The selected project skill root contains 19 ai-sdlc-loop-* directories. Local workflow state appears below .ai-sdlc-loop/<feature>/ and durable machine artifacts use TOON.

docs.title: If installation stops
docs.text:
Loop fails closed on unsafe roots, symlink escapes, occupied unmanaged targets, or drifted managed skills. Read the reported path, preserve local edits, and resolve the conflict before retrying.

Continue with How it works.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Flow is the guided entrypoint; Orchestrate is the direct stage router. Both preserve ownership:

Explore → Apply handoff → Specify → approval → Implement → Verify → approval → Commit
                         ↘ review / QA / security / release controls as required

Explore and Doctor are read-only. Apply confirms one route but does not execute the owner action. Specify persists bounded scope. Implement and Commit validate separate fingerprint-bound approval receipts. Verify executes only declared argv-safe commands and records redacted TOON evidence.

See Contracts for exact schema and authority boundaries.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Complete one repository change with explicit scope, verification evidence, and separate implementation and commit approvals.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use Loop when the request needs a safe coding cycle but does not need the complete AI SDLC Harness discovery and refinement catalog.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3 and Git are available.
  • Loop is installed and verified for the project.
  • The intended source paths and validation commands can be identified.
  • A human or authorized host can provide approval decisions.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Ask for ai-sdlc-loop-orchestrate and describe the bounded outcome.
  2. Review the normalized request, allowed paths, trace IDs, and specification fingerprint.
  3. Approve or reject implementation explicitly.
  4. Review the resulting changed paths before verification.
  5. Run the declared tests and checks through Verify.
  6. Review readiness, redacted evidence, and the verified fingerprint.
  7. Approve or reject the commit separately.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: Confirm that the feature state and evidence are TOON, all changed paths are in scope, every required command passed, and the resulting commit contains the expected traceability.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Approval rejected as stale: regenerate the relevant fingerprint after reviewing drift.
  • Out-of-scope path: stop and update the specification; do not widen scope implicitly.
  • Verification not ready: resolve the named failing or missing command and rerun Verify.
  • Installer reports drift: preserve the local skill edit and review it before replacement.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Explain installation health or package drift without modifying the project.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use Doctor after verification failure, local skill edits, missing runtime files, or before a package upgrade.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Know the installed profile and custom skill root when using agent-project.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Run the installed doctor.py check command with the project root and profile. For an upgrade preview, run upgrade-plan with a trusted local package checkout.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: The report uses ai-sdlc-loop-doctor-report/v1. Every failure includes remediation. Upgrade plans use ai-sdlc-loop-upgrade-plan/v1 and report apply_authorized: false.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: An unreadable or missing install record requires review before reinstalling. Digest drift may represent valuable local edits; preserve it before any approved replacement.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Request a separate approval for any repair or upgrade action recommended by Doctor.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Deliver one bounded repository change with reviewable scope, explicit approvals, and verification evidence.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use this after Loop installation when the work does not require the full Harness discovery and refinement catalog.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Identify the requested outcome, a safe feature slug, likely paths, and relevant verification commands.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Use ai-sdlc-loop-flow to Explore the request.
  2. Review its owner, blockers, planned writes, and fingerprint.
  3. Apply the current route and let the selected owner Specify the change.
  4. Approve implementation only after reviewing the spec fingerprint.
  5. Verify the changed paths and explicit commands.
  6. Approve commit separately only after reviewing current evidence.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: Confirm all durable artifacts are TOON, changed paths remain in scope, required commands passed, and the commit contains the expected traceability.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Route drift requires a new Explore card. Spec or evidence drift requires a new owning-stage approval. Out-of-scope changes stop the loop.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Use Prepare a release when the commit is ready for distribution.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Select one current Loop owner without guessing skill order or broadening authority.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use Flow for a new request, ambiguous next step, or full-flow handoff review.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Loop is installed; the intent and lowercase kebab-case feature slug are known.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Run Explore through the installed flow.py with --intent, --feature, and the appropriate rigor flag. Save the TOON card only when a later Apply is needed. Review it, then run Apply against the same repository. --execute --approve confirms only the handoff selection.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: The Apply artifact uses ai-sdlc-loop-flow-apply/v1, matches the decision fingerprint, selects one owner, and reports owner_action_executed: false.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: FLOW_ROUTE_DRIFT means intent, evidence, route, or owner files changed. Run Explore again. A missing owner requires installation repair, not an implicit fallback.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Follow the selected owning skill and honor every downstream approval gate.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Install and verify the exact Loop package without replacing unrelated skills.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use this guide for a new project or a new supported agent profile.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Review Prerequisites and choose one profile from Supported environments.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Use the one-command install from Start here. Run its separate verification command. For a local checkout, use python3 install.py PROFILE.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: The verifier reports 19 Loop skills and the selected project root contains the exact inventory from the skill catalog.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If unmanaged or drifted content is reported, preserve the local files and run Doctor before deciding whether to replace anything.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with Deliver a first change.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Produce a commit-bound release decision with complete validation evidence.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Use this after implementation, QA, review, and security evidence are current.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: The exact candidate commit is known and every required gate has an owner and evidence.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Run release readiness for the exact commit. Review blockers, residual risks, documentation status, compatibility, and rollback notes. Obtain explicit approval before tag creation, push, or hosted release publication.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: The release artifact is canonical TOON, binds every gate to the same commit, and cannot report ready while a blocker or incomplete gate remains.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Refresh stale evidence against the candidate commit. Do not waive a failed gate by changing only the summary status.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Use the repository release workflow only after the separate external-write approval.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: AI SDLC Loop is experimental. The source tree is preparing v0.2.0; schema changes require a new version and migration notes.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text: Loop controls a small local delivery cycle. It does not reduce or cap model requests, authenticate reviewer identity cryptographically, replace human review, provide hosted orchestration, or automatically push, deploy, release, or open pull requests.

docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.text: Runtime state is local, commands run without a shell, paths are contained, and common secret patterns are redacted before evidence is persisted. Review the repository security policy before processing sensitive work.

docs.title: Later
docs.text:
• Evaluate migration guidance from earlier experimental schemas.
  • Extend compatibility fixtures when Harness promotion contracts change.
  • Stabilize public schemas only after real project feedback.

Loop intentionally does not absorb the full Harness discovery, refinement, role, adoption, or hosted orchestration surface.

docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.text:
Loop keeps workflow state local, invokes verification commands without a shell, contains project paths, and redacts common secret patterns from persisted evidence. It does not provide cryptographic reviewer identity or organizational authorization.

Flow and Doctor are read-only. Doctor remediation and upgrade plans never self-apply. Source mutation, commands, commits, tags, pushes, releases, and deployments remain subject to the owning skill, host sandbox, repository policy, and explicit user authority.

Report vulnerabilities through the repository security advisory form.

docs.title: Runtime commands
docs.text:
The shared CLI exposes specify, approve, implement-check, verify, commit, promote, and status:

python3 .agents/skills/ai-sdlc-loop-shared-runtime/scripts/loop.py --help

docs.title: Durable formats
docs.text: Loop-owned specifications, state, approvals, evidence, install records, review artifacts, release decisions, and promotion output use canonical TOON. JSON-named durable output is rejected.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
Source --help output is authoritative.

Purpose Command Install local checkout python3 install.py PROFILE Verify installation python3 install.py verify PROFILE Shared lifecycle CLI python3 .agents/skills/ai-sdlc-loop-shared-runtime/scripts/loop.py --help Guided Flow python3 .agents/skills/ai-sdlc-loop-flow/scripts/flow.py --help Installation Doctor python3 .agents/skills/ai-sdlc-loop-doctor/scripts/doctor.py --help

Flow exposes explore and apply. Doctor exposes check and upgrade-plan. Custom agents replace .agents/skills with their recorded project-relative skills root.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Contract Schema Authority Guided decision ai-sdlc-loop-flow/v1 Read-only evidence Flow handoff ai-sdlc-loop-flow-apply/v1 Selects one owner; executes no owner action Doctor report ai-sdlc-loop-doctor-report/v1 Read-only evidence Upgrade plan ai-sdlc-loop-upgrade-plan/v1 Planning only; apply is false Install record ai-sdlc-loop-install/v1 Verification evidence Lifecycle state ai-sdlc-loop/v1 Local stage state and fingerprints Promotion ai-sdlc-harness-promotion/v1 Compatibility artifact only

Canonical Loop machine artifacts use deterministic TOON. Fingerprints detect drift; they do not authenticate people or bypass host policy.

docs.title: Supported environments
docs.text:
Profile Skills root Invocation codex-project .agents/skills POSIX bootstrap or Python claude-code-project .claude/skills POSIX bootstrap or Python agent-project Explicit safe relative root POSIX bootstrap or Python with --skills-root

CI validates Python 3.11 on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The runtime uses the Python standard library and Git. The POSIX bootstrap is not the native Windows path; use python install.py there.
